articles.title: European Championship Darts: Luke Woodhouse hits nine-darter and sets up second-round clash with defending champion Gian van Veen
articles.summary: Luke Woodhouse hit a nine-darter in his round one match against Dirk van Duijvenbode; Faces Gian van Veen in second round; Tournament runs from October 22-25; watch the Grand Slam of Darts live on Sky Sports from November 14-22
articles.body:
The perfect nine for Woodhouse came in the fourth leg and against the throw, two 180s being followed by a T20, T19, then accurate D12 to finish it off.

Woodhouse managed to recompose himself immediately and from there held his throw well before finishing off the contest with a bullseye finish.

He will now face Gian van Veen after the defending champion battled hard to a 6-4 win against Andrew Gilding.

"It felt really good," Woodhouse told ITV Sport .

"I had a chance at the Worlds and that didn't go very well.

"I know it is a cliché, but the important thing is the win, so I tried to keep myself calm and crack on with the game.

"I am feeling really good at the moment, I have had a very good year. I didn't want to be one of those people who hit a nine-darter then lost the game."

Van Veen had a tougher night than his round two opponent as he came up against a high-scoring Gilding who was hitting maximums for fun.

The Dutchman held his throw in the ninth leg and then came up with the crucial break of throw on D8 for the match and the chance to continue to defend his title and become the first back-to-back winner since 2018.

Gerwyn Price dispatched two-time champion Rob Cross with a strong 6-2 showing in a battle of former world champions.

The Welshman reeled off four legs in a row from 1-1 before Cross could hit back, a 127 checkout on the bull in the first leg and a 135 finish in the last bookending a stellar showing.

He will now face Cameron Menzies who was clinical in a 6-3 victory over the in-form fourth seed Neils Zonneveld.

The Scotsman found three big breaks of throw that gave him breathing room and with 87 for the match, he held his nerve to take out the bullseye for his spot in the second round.

Elsewhere, top seed Ross Smith survived a scare to pull off a 6-4 victory over Karel Sedlacek.

Once the scores were level at 1-1, it was a game of breaks of throw as both players scored well but struggled on the doubles.

That was the undoing of both players and in a nervy 10th leg, Smith was the one who eventually landed the final dart in D2 for the first hold of throw since the second leg.

In the second round he will play Damon Heta after the Australian pulled off a nervy 6-5 win over 2018 European Champion James Wade to make it through to the second round of the European Championship.

It looked as though Wade had the match in his grasp when he moved 5-3 ahead with a massive 103 checkout on D16.

However, Heta rallied and took the next three legs in a row, shaky finishing from both players seeing him eventually clinch the game on D4.

Meanwhile, Stephen Bunting came up with a clutch 160 finish to win a last-leg thriller against Danny Noppert.

Neither player could take control of the contest and with the game poised at 5-5 all and the throw in his favour, Noppert was waiting to return on for 40 for the win when Bunting showed his class with the stunning T20, T20, then D20 checkout.

Next up, he will face Kim Huybrechts after he reeled off six legs in a row in a brilliant 6-1 demolition of Ryan Searle.

Huybrechts was a late replacement for Luke Humphries who had to withdraw due to illness, but his rushed three-hour drive did not show as he scored with ease, averaged 103.81, and did not allow Searle to get back into the contest.

articles.title: Marlon Humphrey on Ja'Marr Chase: It would be cool if I didn't match up with him so much
articles.summary: Humphrey and Chase have faced off nine times. In those games, Chase has torched the Ravens for 77 catches for 1,245 yards and eight touchdowns.
articles.body:
Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey has covered Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase many times. Maybe more times than he'd like.

Humphrey and Chase have faced off eight times in the regular season and once in the playoffs. In those nine games, Chase has torched the Ravens for 77 catches for 1,245 yards and eight touchdowns.

The Ravens and Bengals will meet again on Sunday, and Humphrey said today that covering Chase and fellow Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins is a big challenge, and one of the toughest assignments an NFL cornerback can draw.

"It would be cool if I didn't match up with him so much," Humphrey said. "He's obviously one of the best in the game. Tee is right up there with him, in the Top 10, I think, in this league. There will be plays made, I think the biggest thing going into this matchup is to try to win more than they win and try to limit the explosives. That's the biggest thing when you're guarding those Top 10, Top 5 guys. It's an all-hands-on-deck game. We look forward to the challenge. I think it'll be a great opportunity."

Despite the success Chase has had against him, Humphrey said he's eager for a big game on Sunday between the 4-2 Ravens and 3-2 Bengals.

"I'm very confident. I think we've had some tests this year, but this will be by far the biggest test yet," Humphrey said.

If Chase's past is any indication, it's going to be a very big test for Humphrey and the Ravens' secondary.

articles.title: Giants’ J.J. McCarthy drops game-changing Jaxson Dart revelation as he replaces Jameis Winston
articles.summary: The New York Giants recently announced that JJ McCarthy would be replacing Jameis Winston as the team’s starting quarterback for this week’s game against the...
articles.body:
The New York Giants recently announced that JJ McCarthy would be replacing Jameis Winston as the team's starting quarterback for this week's game against the Houston Texans. The news comes after McCarthy took over for Winston down the stretch of last week's game vs the New Orleans Saints and nearly led the team on a miraculous comeback.

Now, McCarthy has spoken about his relationship with Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart , whose injury opened the door for Winston to become the starter in the first place.

"I talked to him today, just normal conversation. We're both just rooting for each other. And like I told him, I'm doing the same thing that you want, is help win the football games for this organization and do everything we can and be the best versions of ourselves every day to help the collective," he said, per Giants.com.

McCarthy also spoke on how Dart is helping him out with the X's and O's ahead of his first start in New York.

"It's going to be great because he is such a smart player and obviously very well-rounded in this offense. It's going to be awesome to just ask him really anything and pick his brain about anything," he said.

McCarthy was acquired by the Giants from the Minnesota Vikings earlier this season shortly after Dart's injury, giving New York an insurance policy in case Winston's struggles continued, which they certainly did.

McCarthy overcame an early interception to put up some elite production against the Saints down the stretch on Sunday, nearly pulling off a comeback for the ages in that one.

Now, he'll be matched up against a Texans defense that was arguably the best in the league last year and has now started to round back into form this year.

articles.title: McDermott calls for Super League to accept NRL investment
articles.summary: England head coach Brian McDermott calls for Super League to accept investment from Australia's NRL in order to improve the English game.
articles.body:
England head coach Brian McDermott has called for Super League to accept investment from Australia's NRL in order to improve the English game.

Talks are currently ongoing after Super League clubs rejected a £35m package from the Australian Rugby League Commission and a second deadline of 15 October was allowed to pass without an agreement being reached.

Formalising a partnership between the sport's two leading competitions is seen as as a key step in helping to grow the European competition's revenue.

"I think the NRL's investment in Super League could be very, very positive," said McDermott, who is also the assistant coach of the Gold Coast Titans.

"The product's brilliant. It has always being brilliant. The product's never been the problem. The players have never been the problem. The coaches have never been the problem.

"It's just how it's marketed and how it's presented to people. I think there's some dominoes could start falling our way if the NRL invests and we accept their investment."

Super League is yet to agree a new title sponsorship deal, finalise broadcast negotiations or even its fixtures for the 2027 campaign with London Broncos' position yet to be fully determined.

The Broncos came in16th on the yearly grading list, below fellow Championship side Barrow Raiders, despite a season in which they won the second tier's Grand Final, the 1895 Cup and were runaway champions in the regular-season standings.

The Broncos were overlooked 12 months ago when Bradford Bulls, York Knights and Toulouse Olympique joined the expanded 14-team competition.

But with the backing of Australian businessman Grant Wechsel and former Brisbane Broncos star Darren Lockyer, and with a squad full of internationals, they do still harbour hopes of playing in Super League in 2027.

It is understood any completed deal would involve the Australian governing body insisting on Broncos featuring in the top flight in the near future.

The financial gulf between the northern and southern hemisphere's elite competitions was laid bare, when the NRL struck a record $5.3bn (£3.97bn) television deal over seven years in July.

Super League's TV deal with Sky Sports, which expired at the end of 2026, was worth around £21.5m per year.

"I know there's some positive notes around Super League at the moment, especially with crowds," McDermott added.

"It's been a really interesting competition this year and Wakefield winning the Grand Final puts a brilliant marker down that all the teams can win it.

"It would be a real positive validation of Super League if the NRL were to invest."

McDermott also stressed that an injection of finance into the English game would help widen the pool of talent for future England coaches to call upon. NRL clubs have oversight of players in several age groups leading up first-grade level.

"The TV deal that the NRL's just signed is enormous and [with that you get] preparation, the facilities and the teams coming through that support each NRL club.

"I don't think Super League clubs could populate three teams underneath them with a genuine six, seven, nine and one [the spine of the team].

"So you end up playing a version of rugby league in the UK at junior level, which is good, it's well coached, it's dedicated and it's full of commitment. But you don't have the genuine six, seven, nine and one influence over a game. This is not a new opinion. This has been going on for a long time.

"If you're asking me, is there a big divide between the competitions? Yeah, there is. It's nothing to do with commitment, nothing to do with good-quality coaching or commitment from players. It's just the size of the competitions and the standing in their country."

Goaltender Jacob Markström, who has started six games for Florida this season, is currently out due to an upper-body injury .

articles.title: Notre Dame’s Hannah Hidalgo is a Preseason AP All-American
articles.summary: Notre Dame’s Hannah Hidalgo, the preseason ACC Player of the Year, is now a preseason AP All-American.
articles.body:
In some of the most unsurprising news bits of the day… Notre Dame's Hannah Hidalgo was named as a Preseason AP All-American.

SOUTH BEND, Ind. – Senior guard Hannah Hidalgo has been selected as a Preseason AP All-American, adding another honor to her decorated career. Already named the Preseason ACC Player of the Year earlier this month, Hidalgo enters her senior season at Notre Dame as one of the nation's premier players after putting together one of the most statistically dominant seasons in college basketball history a year ago. She led the ACC in scoring at 25.3 points per game and the nation in steals at 5.6 per game, while averaging 6.9 rebounds and 5.2 assists per contest. She is the only men's or women's college basketball player this century to average at least 25 points, five rebounds, five assists and five steals per game. Her 202 steals set an NCAA single-season record. Hidalgo has also joined an exclusive group of four major-conference players this century to record at least 2,000 points, 500 rebounds, 400 assists and 400 steals in a career: Alana Beard (Duke), Shernise Johnson (Miami) and Armintie Price (Ole Miss). Hidalgo is the first to reach those milestones before completing her junior season. Notre Dame opens the season with an exhibition against Truman State on Oct. 26 at 7 p.m. ET inside Purcell Pavilion before beginning the regular season against Villanova on Nov. 1 at noon ET at the Eternal City Tip-Off in Rome on FS1.

articles.title: Florida Panthers rookie goalie Cooper Black — all 6-feet-9 of him — makes NHL history in debut
articles.summary: PITTSBURGH (AP) — Florida Panthers goalie Cooper Black skated onto the PPG Paints Arena ice alone during pregame warmups on Thursday night, a time-honored ho...
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH (AP) — Florida Panthers goalie Cooper Black skated onto the PPG Paints Arena ice alone during pregame warmups on Thursday night, a time-honored hockey tradition given to rookies everywhere.

It took Black fewer strides to make the memorable lap than most.

Call it one of the upsides of being 6-foot-9.

Black made NHL history in his first career start when he became the tallest goaltender to ever appear in a regular-season game. Black is listed as two inches taller than Ben Bishop, Ivan Fedotov, Mads Sogaard and Mikko Koskinen, all 6-foot-7.

The 25-year-old from Alpen, Michigan, who started playing when he was 8 and had a 5-inch growth spurt between his junior and senior years in high school when he shot up from 6-0 to 6-5 and kept right on going, was excellent in his first period.

Black, called up from Florida's AHL affiliate in Charlotte recently after Jacob Markstrom went down with a shoulder injury, stopped Pittsburgh Penguins defenseman Kris Letang with his blocker pad on a wrist shot about two minutes in. He also turned aside a breakaway opportunity by Penguins forward Rickard Rakell before giving up a goal to Nick Robertson, who beat Black to the glove side.

Panthers head coach Paul Maurice praised Black's development in recent years. Florida signed Black as an undrafted rookie free agent in 2024. Black blossomed last season in Charlotte, posting a 25-13-4 record with a 2.47 goals against average and a .903 save percentage.

"A man that size, it takes a long time to grow into that body," Maurice said before adding with a laugh, "I think he's done."

articles.title: Former NHL player and longtime Rangers fan favorite Ron Duguay dies at 69
articles.summary: Ron Duguay, whose long, wavy hair made him stick out on the ice during an era when helmets were not mandatory in hockey and who played nearly 1,000 games in...
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Ron Duguay, whose long, wavy hair made him stick out on the ice during an era when helmets were not mandatory in hockey and who played nearly 1,000 games in the NHL from the late 1970s through the '80s, has died of cancer. He was 69.

Duguay for several years has been dating Alaska governor and 2008 Republican U.S. vice presidential nominee Sarah Palin, who announced his death after being by his side throughout the illness. A spokesperson for the New York Rangers also confirmed Thursday that Duguay's family informed the team of his passing.

"It's with a shattered heart but also deep peace knowing Ron is with Jesus now," Palin posted on social media. "He fought so hard. Love never ends."

Duguay's first six seasons came as a fan favorite with the Rangers, including an appearance in the 1979 Stanley Cup Final, after they selected him with the 13th pick in the '77 draft.

The Sudbury, Ontario, native was an All-Star as a point-a-game producer in 1981-82.

A series of trades led him to spend time with the Detroit Red Wings, Pittsburgh Penguins and Los Angeles Kings with another Rangers stint, as well. Duguay finished his career in the league with 673 points in the regular season and playoffs, then played in Germany and the minors.

"The New York Rangers organization mourns the loss of Ron Duguay, one of the most popular players in franchise history," the club said in a statement. "Ron's signature skating style — with his hair flowing as he moved down the ice — captivated the (Madison Square) Garden faithful, and his skill, tenacity and charisma earned him the admiration of all New Yorkers. We join the hockey community in sending our condolences to Ron's friends, family and loved ones during this difficult time."

Palin and Duguay's daughter, Shay Thomas, posted several times over the past several months asking for prayers for him. His family started a GoFundMe earlier this year to offset the costs of travel and treatments.

The NHL Alumni Association in a post memorializing Duguay called his dedication and passion for hockey unwavering.

"It was a part of who he was, a lifelong love that he carried with pride and shared so generously with others," the NHLAA said. "He will be remembered not only for the player he was, but for the extraordinary person he was."

Long after his playing days, Duguay was known to another generation of Rangers fans for his role on broadcasts from 2007-18.

articles.title: Texas' Steve Sarkisian could end up benching Arch Manning. Who could be his replacement?
articles.summary: Texas could turn to KJ Lacey, a talented sophomore backup if Arch Manning struggles in another SEC contest in Saturday's home game vs. No. 7 Ole Miss.
articles.body:
Steve Sarkisian hoped to send Arch Manning to New York in December for the annual Heisman Trophy ceremony. The Texas football head coach may instead send his starting quarterback to the bench before the end of October.

Sarkisian said Thursday he wouldn't rule out a removal of Manning from his starting spot Saturday against Ole Miss . Sarkisian's comments continued his stance from both Monday and last Saturday, when he said all players, including Manning, will have their roles evaluated after Texas' 27-24 loss to Florida .

"Every game is different, ya know?" Sarkisian said regarding a potential quarterback change. "I think Arch has had a good week of work, he's prepared himself well, but like the team, he needs to play well. And we'll go from there."

Why the possible move from Arch Manning?

Manning's starting spot is increasingly in question after a difficult first three weeks of SEC play. Manning has four turnovers and four touchdown passes in Texas' three games against Tennessee, Oklahoma and Florida, contests that included critical turnovers from Manning in the final minutes of the fourth quarter.

Sarkisian didn't shy away from criticizing his quarterback this week. Manning himself isn't above harsh self reflection, which he paired with a note of positivity Monday.

"I fully expect myself to play better. I haven't put good film on tape the past five weeks," Manning said. "I'm going to be better. I'm going to be better for teammates, be better for myself, be better for my coaches. This team is built for adversity. I'm built for adversity, and we're going to respond. I know that."

Who could replace Arch Manning on Saturday?

Manning joined Texas as one of the highest-rated high school recruits in history. His potential replacement wasn't quite as hyped, though he brings his own set of impressive accolades. Sophomore KJ Lacey committed to Texas as a four-star recruit in 2023, then arrived on campus in January 2025. He threw for the second-most yards in Alabama high school history and he was Alabama's "Mr. Football" award winner in 2024.

Lacey, a 6-foot, 188-pound right-hander, has nine career college passes in three games across the past two seasons. He completed six of seven passes for 55 yards in the second half of Texas' Week 1 win over Texas State and he completed his lone completion in a Week 3 win over UTSA.

"KJ is a good player. I mean, he's dynamic with the ball in his hands. He's a natural passer," Sarkisian said Thursday. "There's always things, nuances when you lack experience in practice, and we put him in some difficult situations. There's some growing pains that come with that, but he's coachable. He brings a good attitude every day. I think he's got good rapport with his teammates."

Manning will start Saturday, per Sarkisian. Perform well in the first half, and his starting spot should remain safe. But continued struggles for Manning could send him to the bench, perhaps ushering in a new era for the Longhorns at quarterback.

articles.title: Everything Texans DC Matt Burke said ahead of Week 7 game vs Giants
articles.summary: Here's everything Houston Texans defensive coordinator Matt Burke said on Thursday ahead of Week 7's matchup against the New York Giants, including the game...
articles.body:
Here's everything Houston Texans defensive coordinator Matt Burke said on Thursday ahead of Week 7's matchup against the New York Giants , including the game plan of slowing down Malik Nabers, the change at quarterback to J.J. McCarthy and the change of the defense in the past several weeks.

On New York Giants WR Malik Nabers and TE Isaiah Likely

"They're both really good, really productive players. I'll start with Nabers. Both of them, I think they're the top, most targeted duo in the league from just a two-man show. Nabers, I never have gone against them until we started looking at them this year, he has it all in his bag. The route tree's open for him. They do a lot in terms of getting him the ball in the RPO game and some of the screen game, the intermediate stuff, just the individual routes on the backside. Obviously, he's got a lot of down-the-field plays as well. Made a couple big catches last week. I think he's got 35 targets in the last two weeks. So obviously, someone that they're trying to feature, they're going to get him the ball in a lot of different ways and he can do it all. There's not any level of the route tree that's not open to him. It'll be a fun challenge. Then Likely, we've obviously matched up against Baltimore a lot since we've been here the last three, four years. Really seen him grow a lot. Just from where we've seen him and his role going against him the last few years, I think he's improved a lot since I've seen him. He's heavily involved, particularly in the third-down red zone, those types of areas. He's really getting a lot of work there. They're similar, again, they're running option routes and underneath stuff with him. You can see the sort of [Travis] Kelce, not comparing them, but just how they're using him from some Kansas City influence in terms of the way they're trying to get him open. He's become a really, really big weapon. They're two big challenges for us that we're looking forward to going against this week."

Q: On S M.J. Stewart in Week 6 vs. Jacksonville

"He did a great job for us. M.J.'s played a lot of ball for us, especially last year in particular. His journey coming back from that and having to come in on PUP and all that stuff. Just have a lot of trust in him and how he prepares. Probably asks the most questions of anybody in the meetings and stuff. He always wants to be on it. I think it shows up when he goes out and plays for us. So did a really good job. All those veteran guys that have come and stepped in for us. Tremon [Smith], another one. Both those guys did a really good job helping us win that ball game."

Burke: "Obviously, he came in, did a really good job sparking them to a little bit of a comeback and getting them back in that game last week. Another person who made a lot of big plays. Then just trying to go back a little bit just to see what he likes to do and what he's comfortable with and sort of what his strengths are just from generic tape. Obviously, not schematically. That's a little different from what they're doing in Minnesota. So yeah, we've gone back and tried to see just where we think there's always a little bit of projection. We always kind of go back to, let's make sure we're doing what we need to be doing. But really athletic, gets out, made a few plays with his legs, both scrambling and then obviously buying time in the pocket. That's another factor we've got to account for. Even early in the season in New York, they were putting them in some packages to run some quarterback runs and stuff. That's another thing that we're sort of trying to make sure we're on top of. We're trying to go back and just make sure we're crossing all our T's and dotting our I's to make sure we have a good sense of what we're about to face."

Q: On whether the five-man defensive front is to help DT Kayden McDonald see more game action

Burke: "I think that's sort of a byproduct of that. I think when we're scheming up how we want to do things, it has been good for us. We've done it since we've been here, just different versions of it. 'K-Mac's' done a really good job of kind of owning that role and trying to build out a little niche for him since he's been back. He's done a really good job in the two weeks he's been playing, just being stout, being square, making some plays in the run game, trying to eat up space. It was good to kind of get him going again, but it's not like an exclusive reason that we're doing that if we think that putting those guys out there. Teams have kind of gone back to some 13 and some extra tight end personnel groups and those sort of things. So, it's just week to week, if that's a tool that we think can help combat some of the things we're seeing in those personnel groupings, then we'll deploy that. We're fortunate that we've been able to play some more base too, having Henry [To'oTo'o]and Jake [Hansen] back and those guys. Now we've got some different groupings that we can kind of mix and match depending on how we feel is a good fit for what we're seeing."

Q: On the value of defensive tackles taking up space

Burke: "You're just trying to basically clog and run lanes, I guess you would say. Especially when you're going in those big personnel groupings and you're getting two tight ends and three tight ends and two tight ends and a full back and all those things, it's creating more, they're trying to create more gaps in there. They're extending the line by putting three tight ends out there or they're putting a full back in the backfield to create an extra gap wherever he's fitting. That's creating a second gap whenever he's running through a B-gap or whatnot. To combat that, when you have a guy like Kayden [McDonald], [Jaden] Crumedy done a really good job. Obviously, we know Tommy [Togiai] has always done that for us in terms of just sort of eating that space up and trying to close some of those windows down. We talk about filling up space and eating space, like you close some of those gaps down and it takes away some of that advantage from an offensive perspective. I think all of our interior guys have done a really good job of sort of understanding the run schemes that we're getting week to week and trying to sort of close some of those windows down a little bit."

Burke: "I think I would say our tackling, issues isn't the right word, but some of our tackling issues were, I would debate anybody that says we're not a physical team. I think like just a lot of it is getting to the right spots and your leaving feet behind, being behind a tackle where you're kind of swinging off and those sorts of things. In practice, I feel like the emphasis has been sort of getting in front and positionally. Not being on a side tackle or being behind, or again, not leaving your feet to go make the play because that's when you lose your power. I know we're not bringing guys down or really striking people out here, but I wouldn't say that's been our problem. Our problem has maybe been we have to take that extra step to get our body in front of somebody and not be on a side tackle or sort of swinging off. The emphasis has been sort of taking those extra steps, getting into positionally in the right spot to be able to tackle. Then I think that the physical nature will show up on Sundays."

Q: On facing an offense that utilizes the fullback position

Burke: "I'd say it's almost like a hybrid offense with Coach [Greg] Roman's influence and obviously Coach [Matt] Nagy. You've got some of the gap schemes and the two-back runs and those sorts of things. But then there are also some, I would say, Kansas City influence, RPOs and that sort of thing too. You try to sort of balance all that. They've had some different approaches in different games and sort of which way they're leaning on some of that stuff. Generically, anytime that you're playing a coordinator or a scheme or a head coach that you have a history with, you have to obviously go back and make sure that things that they've utilized against you in the past are sound and cleaned up from what we're seeing. This is probably a pretty diverse offense in that sense, in terms of making sure that we're checking off all our boxes."

Q: On how the defensive communication has changed with Head Coach DeMeco Ryans calling defensive plays

Burke: "Yeah, I don't know. We're 2-0. Hopefully that's something. On game days, it's really just been a back-and-forth street. You'd have to ask him from his point of view. There's a lot of communication, a lot of like, 'Hey, what do we think here? What about this?' I always try to just have my answers ready for him to provide the information that he might need to make his final decision. I think our communication has been really good. I think we're trying to streamline everything with the players and make sure that we're in the right spots."

Q: On whether he saw former Texan J.J. Watt working in broadcast

Burke: "Obviously, he's got into it pretty quickly after he was done playing. I keep in touch with J.J. a lot and talk to him fairly frequently. I think whatever J.J. chooses to do, he's going to excel at. I think when he commits himself to doing something, he's going to commit to greatness. I don't really get to watch a lot of his games because we're usually busy at the same time, but it doesn't surprise me that he's excelling and having success in whatever he's doing. A little shout-out: his son's birthday is tomorrow. Happy Birthday, Koa."

Mike Vrabel is in his 27th season as a player or coach in the NFL.

Yet, tonight marks his first career regular-season game at Soldier Field.

Larry Mayer of the Bears' team website reported this stat that seems impossible.

Vrabel played for the Steelers (1997-2000), Patriots (2001-08) and Chiefs (2009-10); he was an assistant for the Texans (2014-17); and he was the head coach of the Titans (2018-23) and Patriots (2025-present).

He never played and has never coached in the NFC, which limits the number of times his teams have gone against the Bears on the road.

The only previous away game Vrabel had against the Bears was in 2002 as a player for the Patriots. The Bears, though, played their home games in Champaign, Illinois, that season while Soldier Field was being renovated.

As Ben Volin of the Boston Globe points out, Vrabel's Titans played preseason games at Soldier Field in 2019 and 2023.

The New York Rangers are one of the most surprising teams in the NHL through the early part of the season as they are in second place in the Metropolitan Division, just two points behind the Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes.

In an effort to improve the overall depth of their forward group, the Rangers have signed Luke Glendening after the 13-year NHL veteran had a professional try out with the team.

Glendening has played center at many points in his career, but he can also play on the wing. The 37-year-old has primarily been a defensive player throughout his career. He has never scored more than 12 goals in a season. He has not scored in double figures since the 2018-19 season when he scored 10 goals while playing for the Detroit Red Wings.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Glendening spent 10 years with the Red Wings, two years with the Tampa Bay Lightning, two years with the Dallas Stars along with single seasons with the New Jersey Devils and Philadelphia Flyers.

Glendening is knowns for his speed on the ice as well as his ability in the face-off circle. He has connected on 55.6 percent of the draws he has taken throughout his career.

The Rangers will likely use him on their fourth line and as a penalty killer. His speed on the ice allows him to cover much of the defensive zone when his team is shorthanded.

The Rangers have had an issue with their fourth-line center since veteran Joe Veleno went down with a lower-body injury. Glendening will have an excellent chance to fill that role.

articles.title: Preview: Can UND keep it going in Minneapolis?
articles.summary: Oct. 22—MINNEAPOLIS — Minnesota's record isn't fooling UND coach Dane Jackson. After watching game video on the Gophers, Jackson concluded that special teams...
articles.body:
Oct. 22—MINNEAPOLIS — Minnesota's record isn't fooling UND coach Dane Jackson.

After watching game video on the Gophers, Jackson concluded that special teams have gotten Minnesota in trouble at times, but overall, the Gophers are much better than their 0-3-1 record indicates.

"Their 5-on-5 play looks pretty darn good to me," Jackson said. "They've had some goals scored on them on their penalty kill, but overall, there's a lot of good play 5-on-5."

UND and Minnesota are set to renew their rivalry at 7 p.m. Thursday and 6 p.m. Friday in 3M Arena at Mariucci.

UND comes in with a perfect 4-0 record after sweeping Bemidji State and Bentley. Three of the four games were at home.

The Gophers are winless through four games for the first time since 2009-10, but have played the

in the Central Collegiate Hockey Association (Michigan Tech) and the National Collegiate Hockey Conference (Minnesota Duluth). All four games were on the road.

"I just hope we keep building," Minnesota first-year head coach Brett Larson said. "I thought our best game of the year was Saturday night and we want to build off that. I think it gave the guys some confidence that we're learning to play winning hockey, we're learning to play the right way."

Minnesota will now play nine consecutive games at home, beginning with the sold-out homecoming weekend series against UND.

"It's been an incredibly odd schedule in some ways," Larson said. "I think our players are excited to play in front of our fans finally. I think they can't wait to feed off their energy."

One area where UND holds a statistical edge is in the faceoff dot.

The Fighting Hawks have won 61.1% of their faceoffs, ranking No. 1 nationally. The Gophers are at 43%, ranking 54th of the 57 teams that have played.

Minnesota has made slight changes at center from game to game. Last Saturday, L.J. Mooney, Wyatt Cullen, Brooks Cullen and Tanner Ludtke lined up in the middle.

UND's usual centers are Cole Reschny, Ollie Josephson, Hudson Malinoski and Gavin Lindberg.

"We've got to play fast," UND forward Will Zellers said. "That Minnesota team is so highly skilled. They've got a bunch of the top players in the country. If we're turning pucks over and creating their offense for them and not playing too hard, they're going to feed off that."

On the back end, both teams look significantly different than last season.

Five of Minnesota's eight blue liners are new — All-American transfer Evan Murr, transfer Tanner Henricks, transfer Finn Loftus, freshman Axel Löfgren and freshman Tarin Smith, who is nearing a return from an injury he sustained last spring.

Five of UND's eight blue liners are new — transfer Brasen Boser, freshman Carson Carels, freshman Ethan MacKenzie, freshman Garrett Lindberg and freshman Bauer Dumanski.

"With a young group, you've got a lot to teach them details and also bring them together," UND assistant coach Dillon Simpson said. "I've been super proud of how all eight of them have worked and really come to the rink with the mindset to get better and learn. They're super coachable."

Both teams have been good on the power play — a carryover from last season.

UND (37.5%) and Minnesota (28.6%) both rank in the top 11 nationally in power play percentage. Last season, both finished in the top 10.

"You've got to be ready for anything," Jackson said. "There are a lot of emotional swings. It's important to be on the edge, be ready to compete but not go overboard."

Minnesota — D Tarin Smith questionable (upper body)

Minnesota trailed 2-0 last Saturday in Duluth when Ziemer, the captain, took over. He scored back-to-back goals, pulling the Gophers into a tie.

Ziemer, a third-round Buffalo Sabres pick, is coming off a 23-goal sophomore season. Ziemer plays right wing on a line with Mooney and Austin Burnevik, a 20-goal scorer last season at St. Cloud State.

"He's been unbelievable all year, to be honest," Larson said of Ziemer. "He practices like a pro. His detail, his preparation. . . everything is elite. I think we've got a great captain leading us through some tough times here early."

This is a big series for Twin Cities players returning home and UND has a bunch of them on this roster — Zellers (Maple Grove), Jack Kernan (Maple Grove), Cody Croal (North Branch), Ashton Schultz (Excelsior), Cooper Simpson (Shakopee) and Caleb Heil (Victoria).

Some of those players, especially the highly competitive ones, seem to thrive in homecomings. Think Danny Kristo and Jackson Blake. Zellers is a big-game player with a fiercely competitive streak. The last time he returned home — the 2026 World Junior Championship — he lit up the scoresheet.

"It's pretty special to be able to go back there and play only 20 minutes from my house and have a lot of family and friends in the stands," Zellers said.

Too much has been made of the records. It's a small sample size. The Gophers have been on the road playing teams who should make the NCAA tournament. UND has been mostly at home. This will be UND's biggest challenge to date.

There's only been one sweep in this series since November 2011. UND won a pair on Thanksgiving weekend in 2019. Outside of that, there have been a whole lot of splits, and this one has split written all over it.

UND-Minnesota rivalry 'feels like Game 7 of the Stanley Cup Finals'

UND goalie recruit Jakub Husár scores again

articles.summary: Indian squash sensation Anahat Singh continued her giant-killing run at the Silicon Valley Open 2026, producing a remarkable comeback to defeat Egypt's
articles.body: Indian squash sensation Anahat Singh continued her giant-killing run at the Silicon Valley Open 2026, producing a remarkable comeback to defeat Egypt's Salma Hany in a five-game thriller and book her maiden semi-final berth at a PSA Gold-level event. The 18-year-old World No. 15 recovered from a 1-2 deficit to register a 4-11, 11-8, 4-11, 11-2, 11-5 victory over the sixth-seeded Egyptian in 42 minutes in Redwood City, California.Anahat showed tremendous resilience after twice falling behind in the contest, raising her level in the final two games to complete an impressive turnaround. Having conceded the opening and third games, the Indian dominated the closing stages, dropping just seven points across the last two games to seal a landmark win.The victory marks another significant milestone in Anahat's burgeoning career and comes on the back of her stunning second-round upset of eight-time world champion and World No. 3 Nour ElSherbini.Anahat rallies from behind to seal historic victoryHany made a strong start, capitalising on Anahat's errors to take the opening game 11-4. The Indian responded with an improved performance in the second, winning it 11-8 to restore parity.However, the Egyptian regained control in the third game, cruising to another 11-4 win to move within a game of victory. With her quarter-final hopes hanging in the balance, Anahat produced a superb response, stepping up her intensity to dismantle Hany 11-2 in the fourth game.The teenager carried that momentum into the decider, maintaining her composure and dictating the rallies to close out the contest 11-5. Her emphatic finish underlined her ability to respond under pressure against an experienced opponent.The win ensures Anahat reaches the last four of a PSA Gold event for the first time in her career, further strengthening her growing reputation on the international squash circuit.Asian Games final rematch awaits Anahat in semi-finalsAnahat's reward for the hard-fought quarter-final victory is a semi-final showdown against Malaysia's World No. 4 Sivasangari Subramaniam, who booked her place in the last four with a straight-games win over compatriot Rachel Arnold.The clash will renew a rivalry established at the 2026 Asian Games, where Sivasangari defeated Anahat 3-0 in the women's singles final to claim gold, leaving the Indian with silver. Anahat had made history at the continental event by becoming the first Indian woman to reach the squash singles final.Anahat has enjoyed an impressive campaign in Redwood City. articles.title: Todd Benzinger, who caught the final out of the Reds' 1990 World Series sweep, dead at 63
articles.summary: Todd Benzinger, the first baseman who caught the final out of the Cincinnati Reds' 1990 World Series sweep over the Oakland Athletics, died at 63.
articles.body: Todd Benzinger, the first baseman who caught the final out of the Cincinnati Reds’ 1990 World Series sweep, died Wednesday at age 63. His cause of death has not been released. A Cincinnati-area native, Benzinger was drafted out of high school by the Boston Red Sox in 1981. After two seasons in Boston, he was traded to his hometown Reds ahead of the 1989 season. His defining career moment came on Oct. 20, 1990, when he caught the game-ending out in foul territory against the Oakland Athletics, securing Cincinnati's most recent title. The Reds posted on X: "The Cincinnati Reds are saddened by the passing of former first baseman and 1990 World Series champion Todd Benzinger. Todd will be remembered with great affection and gratitude for his place in one of the most memorable chapters in Reds history. Our deepest condolences go out to his family, friends, former teammates and all who knew and loved him." The Reds traded Benzinger to the Kansas City Royals in 1991. He retired after the 1995 season, finishing a nine-year major league career with a .257 batting average, 733 hits, and 376 RBIs over 924 games. Benzinger stayed active in local baseball after his playing days, managing Cincinnati's Class-A affiliate, the Dayton Dragons, from 2009 to 2010. "Todd will forever be remembered by Reds fans for catching the final out of the 1990 World Series, but those of us who had the privilege of knowing him will remember so much more," said Rick Walls, executive director of the Reds Hall of Fame and Museum. articles.title: Against the odds, Sheetal Devi reigns supreme with double gold at Asian Para Games
articles.summary: The tears came first, the smiles followed.
articles.body: The tears came first, the smiles followed. As Sheetal Devi stood victorious once again, the emotions of a remarkable journey spilled over at the Okazaki Central Park Multipurpose Square in Nagoya — the venue for para-archery competitions. They were tears of overcoming adversity, of keeping promises made to herself, her family and coaches, and of seeing a year of relentless hard work culminate in gold. The archer had done it again, returning from the Asian Para Games with two gold medals and a silver.The 19-year-old from J&K’s Loidhar village in Kishtwar district produced a stunning double gold performance on Thursday, retaining her women’s compound individual crown before teaming up with Toman Kumar to clinch the mixed team title. She had already won silver in the women’s compound doubles alongside quadruple amputee Payal Nag on Tuesday.The individual final against Singapore’s Alim Nur Syahidah was a test of nerve. Trailing 55-59 after the opening two ends, Sheetal faced a four-point deficit against the 41-year-old Singaporean. But the world No. 1 responded with six 10s, including three arrows landing closest to the bull’s-eye, turning the contest around to lead by two points.With gold within reach, she shot three 9s in the final end. Alim needed a strong finish but managed only 26 points to Sheetal’s 27, handing the Indian a 142-139 a second successive individual gold.Earlier, Sheetal and Toman had beaten Indonesia’s Teodora Audi Ayudia Ferelly and Ken Swagumilang 151-148. After establishing a four-point advantage midway through the final, the Indians absorbed Indonesia’s late challenge and held on for gold. Their combined qualification score of 1,402 had also set a world record. “There was some pressure because of the wind. But my coach told me not to worry and just reset for the next end,” she said after her win. “The silver was also good for me. But the gold I won today, I am happy that what I had set to do, I have done,” she added.Born without arms, Sheetal positions her bow with her feet and legs, drawing and releasing the string with her shoulder and jaw. From winning gold at Hangzhou in 2023 to claiming bronze at the Paris Paralympics, her rise has been extraordinary.India celebrated another medal as Swati Chaudhary won the country’s first-ever W1 archery medal, taking silver after losing 4-6 to China’s Cen Mengkan. articles.title: La historia de Pablo Semprún, el 'Ballesteros' del pádel que enseñó a Aznar y ahora guía a Martina Calvo
articles.standfirst: El considerado primer jugador profesional de pádel en España plantó cara a los argentinos y sentó las bases de una industria en la que fue pionero.
articles.summary: El considerado primer jugador profesional de pádel en España atiende a MARCA para narrar su historia, la de un pionero que plantó cara a los argentinos y ha vuelto años después a la élite para ser entrenador.
articles.body: La historia de Pablo Semprún (Madrid, España, 1964) es un viaje para adentrarse en el ADN del pádel en España. Extenista, se convirtió por accidente en pionero de la primera ola profesional en los 90 cuando el pádel todavía residía en Argentina fagocitando el profesionalismo y tras mucho esfuerzo, triunfó. Alguien que brilló en la pista y trabajó tanto en la sombra por el crecimiento de su deporte que acabó quedándose atrapado en ella durante varias décadas. El backstage de una industria todavía muy prematura fue su terreno de juego durante años tras la retirada y, ahora, temporalmente ha vuelto casi por casualidad a la primera línea reconvertido en la figura de entrenador. Un distinto que no ha cambiado, un outsider en el star system y una figura con conocimiento, vehemencia y liderazgo en el deporte que ahora sirve de guía al nuevo gran talento femenino: Martina Calvo. Pero para entender la trascendencia de Semprún hay que remontarse muchos años atrás. En una España en efervescencia donde La Movida madrileña marcaba el ritmo social, los estragos de la heroína eran una tema de Estado y el Servicio Militar Obligatorio (la mili, vaya) empezaba a tocar a su fin, un ya no tan joven Semprún cambiaría la raqueta de tenis por la paleta sin haberlo buscado para hacer carrera en aquello del pádel. O paddle. “Llego al pádel con 30 años. Antes venía de jugar al tenis profesional, aunque fui un profesional tardío. En aquella época estudiaba empresariales y no era tan fácil decidir que ibas a dedicarte al deporte porque te miraban un poco como diciendo, ¿qué haces? Empecé jugando al pádel por diversión y rápidamente vi que aquello podía ser algo más”, recuerda Semprún a MARCA sobre una bonita, luchada e imprevista historia. Porque aquel deporte nacido por necesidad en Acapulco (México) viviría su primera etapa profesional en Argentina y durante más de 20 años los jugadores argentinos serían los dominadores de la disciplina compitiendo en un fuerte circuito nacional y luciéndose en España un par de veces al año para disputar los dos torneos importantes que se jugaban en el calendario de la Federación y que organizaban las empresas Padel Visión y Padel Team, esta última fundada por Semprún. “Los argentinos estaban cuatro o cinco escalones por encima. No venían prácticamente a jugar torneos internacionales y, cuando nosotros íbamos allí, nos metían 6-0 y 6-1. Si hacíamos un juego ya parecía una heroicidad. Yo vi aquello y pensé: ¡Esto no puede ser!”, explica sobre la hegemonía de los Lasaigues, Gattiker y compañía. Y dicho y hecho. Impetuoso, competitivo y formado, Semprún empezó a sentar las bases de algo más que un juego para poder mirar de tú a tú a las grandes estrellas argentinas y aunque le costaría varios años, iba a lograr cambiar para siempre ya el tablero de juego del pádel junto a otro ilustre de la historia del pádel en España, Alberto Rodríguez Piñón. “El primer año me lo tomé todavía como algo amateur. Me costó dinero, pero empecé a ganar torneos. El segundo año ya ganaba casi todos los torneos nacionales. Y en la tercera tentativa, ya con Piñón, empezamos a hacer las cosas para ser profesionales y aunque no les ganábamos, competíamos”, continúa sobre el proceso. En 1996 llegaría el punto de inflexión. En la tercera edición del Mundial de pádel por parejas Semprún y Piñón conseguirían meterse en la final tras derrotar en semifinales a una de las cabezas de serie favoritas y rozarían la épica. “Para mí aquello es un antes y un después del pádel español. Antes de ese Mundial ya habíamos conseguido ganar a parejas imposibles, pero allí lo hicimos ante ‘Bebe’ Auguste y Mariano Lasaigues, que eran favoritos, y fuimos al tercer set ante Lasaigues y Gattiker teniendo nuestras oportunidades”, rememora con ese sabor agridulce del que sabe la importancia de lo logrado, pero que aún cree que la historia pudo ser diferente. Un fin de semana que marcaría el desarrollo del pádel en España porque por primera vez lo que ocurría dentro del 20x10 tenía repercusión. Y si no que se lo digan a las más de 5.000 personas que se dieron cita en el Club de Campo en Madrid o a los miles de espectadores que siguieron aquellas gestas por primera vez por televisión en Televisión Española cuando, hasta entonces, para ver el pádel en ‘la caja tonta’ “tenías que comprar algunos minutos de espacio para salir en la 2”, recuerda. Pero, más allá de resultados, ¿es Semprún considerado el primer jugador profesional español? Lejos de buscar solo la victoria deportiva, lo cierto es que le dedicó tiempo, esfuerzos y empeño a sentar las bases del primer ecosistema donde el deportista pudiera al menos ganarse la vida ayudando a su vez a que el deporte creciera en popularidad. “A los pocos jugadores españoles que eran buenos, como Arenzana o Fontán, les daban cinco palas al año que luego vendían y estaban felices. Yo empecé a pedir que me pagaran, que no me valía con unas palas y que tenía una serie de gastos para competir”, detalla sobre los que serían los primeros contratos de esponsorización. Ya se sabe que si uno no se pone en valor es difícil que el de enfrente esté dispuesto a ello, que nadie regala nada y menos cuando se habla de dinero. “Fui el primero que planteó que aquello tenía que ser profesional también económicamente y conseguí, a través de muchos contactos, patrocinadores como Telefónica o Caja Madrid que me permitieron tener unos ingresos suficientes para dedicarme al pádel”, continúa. Semprún es una persona bien posicionada socialmente y sus contactos le darían al deporte de la pala acceso a un estrato nuevo que aunque estigmatizaría al pádel en España como “un deporte de pijos” durante años, ayudaría en su popularización vinculándolo a figuras como la de José María Aznar o el entonces príncipe Felipe con el que había estudiado en el colegio. Su apellido por parte paterna le hace descendiente de un linaje aristocrático vinculado a las artes, las letras y la política que se remonta a antes de la República, pero siempre ha buscado manejar sus méritos sin el peso de la historia quizá, sin saberlo, por herencia materna que le hace vivir de forma privada su parte más íntima sin rehuir de la historia. “Sí, yo conseguí que Aznar jugase al pádel y, evidentemente, aunque aquello nos vino muy bien tengo que decir que las ruedas de prensa eran un coñazo porque lo único que preguntaban era si Aznar jugaba o dejaba de jugar”, confiesa sobre una figura que hizo que la palabra pádel se empezara a colar en la sociedad española iniciado ya el nuevo siglo. “Claro que fue un catalizador importante. El pádel se etiquetó como un deporte de pijos, pero Aznar era una figura muy relevante a nivel popular. Yo tenía relación con él y también con presidentes y directivos de algunas empresas y aunque sabía que aquellos contactos eran pasajeros y efímeros, que mis amigos eran otros, eran muy importantes para el deporte”, señala sabedor de la importancia de construir una industria que necesita de músculo económico, popular y relacional. Una vía que abriría al pádel los primeros grandes patrocinios nacionales, las primeras inyecciones de capital, y que le granjeó algunos enemigos. “Yo buscaba patrocinadores y utilicé mis contactos, pero hay algo que quizá sea más importante porque de lo que conseguía destinaba la mitad a la Federación para que fuese fuerte. ¿Me creó problemas? Sí, había envidias, pero yo tenía claro que si quería crecer necesitaba que el deporte creciera y que si no había campeonatos aquello no tenía ningún sentido”, explica. Una realidad, la de buscar y encontrar patrocinios, que bien sabe lo difícil que era Carlos Almazán, otro de los grandes nombres de la época y que lo vivió en primera persona. "Sí, Pablo organizo eventos de pádel que sin duda ayudaron al crecimiento de este deporte en una época en la que no era fácil conseguir patrocinios. Tambien es conocido que ayudó a sus compañeros con patrocinadores en un momento donde era importante contar con recursos para gastos", recuerda Almazán, también miembro del Hall of Fame del pádel español. Y es que Semprún, sin buscar la filantropía, sabía de la importancia de no ser el único jugador profesional. “Además, con ese dinero pude ayudar a muchos jugadores. Te podría decir 10 o 15 jugadores a los que conseguí patrocinadores a través de las marcas y eso, en aquella época, tenía muchísimo mérito porque la notoriedad que tenía el pádel era ridícula. Jugué con Pablo Rovaletti y me decía: Tú eres tonto, ¿por qué les traes a estos nada?”, continúa para, después, dar aún más contexto de cómo era salir a intentar captar algo de inversión para ser profesional. “Recuerdo una anécdota en una reunión que, tras estar una hora hablando con un director de marketing, salimos pensando que había explicado perfectamente lo que era el pádel y que cuando ya me iba me dijera: Oye, te voy a hacer una pregunta personal, ¿por qué los pakistaníes son los mejores en esto?”, confiesa riéndose con una carcajada sincera, uno de esos gestos involuntarios que detectas en alguien que ha viajado en el tiempo al rememorar una época divertida y alegre. Así, construyendo una carrera dentro y fuera de la pista, Semprún se convirtió en una referencia que jugó y ganó mucho con nombres tan conocidos en el pádel como Piñón, Robaletti, Auguste o, incluso, Fernando Belasteguín, el GOAT, que asegura a Marca ⁠que ”de esa época juntos tengo muy lindo recuerdos”. Porque, sí, en 2001 Semprún y un joven Bela compartirían pista logrando cinco títulos y acabarían en segundo lugar del ranking solo por detrás de Juan Martín Díaz y Hernán ‘Bebe’ Auguste. El último capítulo antes de que arrancara la etapa más exitosa del pádel con la hegemonía de 13 años de ‘Los Reyes’. “Es verdad que solo jugué ocho o nueve años y aunque hay gente que ha ganado más que yo, no es algo que me obsesione y me quedo con que he ganado con todos mis compañeros”, repasa sobre una carrera profesional que le hizo ganarse durante años el honor de ser el mejor jugador español de todos los tiempos. Jugador de drive con una de las mejores voleas del circuito, un smash potente y un juego marcado por los cambios de ritmo y la presión constante, su personalidad fuerte y carismática llevaba al límite a rivales y, por qué no decirlo, a compañeros. “Era un jugador con mucho carácter, con muchas virtudes en el juego de ataque y carencias en el fondo de la pista en los golpes de doble pared. Pero en los momentos importantes de los partidos, no sé cómo lo hacía pero lo que no se le daba bien lo hacía perfecto”, explica Bela. Juego aparte, su carácter siempre fue algo imposible de disociar en su figura. Pablo y Semprún son lo mismo. Sin artificios, inteligente, temperamental y competitivo, su forma de competir preparó sin saberlo el terreno de la era más dorada del deporte de la pala. “Pablo fue la persona que me ofreció venir a vivir en el 2001 porque el Mago Sanz le dijo que apostara por mí como compañero. Tenía un carácter muy fuerte y ejercía muchísima presión, pero me sirvió mucho para después jugar con Juan Martín y no sentir nada de presión al jugar con el número uno de esa época”, rememora el ‘Boss’ con sinceridad y reconocimiento. Una etapa que duraría solo un año y tras la que, habiendo ya planteado la retirada y habiendo disfrutado de un nuevo impulso con el argentino, le serviría a Semprún para empezar su adiós al pádel. Al menos, como jugador. La exigencia, el foco mediático y una vida empresarial que empezaba a reclamar más atención serían su carta de despedida de las pistas. “Acabé exhausto. Venía de seis o siete años de tenis y ocho o nueve de pádel, con lo cual hablamos de 16 o 17 años de deporte. Y quería hacer otras cosas, la verdad. Cuando me retiré, con 39 o casi 40, mi empresa estaba creciendo muchísimo, me pedía más y no necesitaba seguir estando en el foco porque, de hecho, no me gusta”, explica sobre la retirada. Así colgó la pala y, aunque siguió compitiendo en veteranos donde ha sido número uno del ranking ITF en tenis y habitual en las convocatorias de España en pádel, la vida deportiva pasó a un segundo plano. En esa etapa se centró en el desarrollo del pádel a nivel empresarial con Padel Team, la empresa con la que organizaba uno de los dos grandes torneos de España en los 90 y que fue clave en el crecimiento nacional siguiendo la estela de Padel Visión, la primera gran promotora fundada por Pablo Neira, Javier Arenzana, Felipe García Quirós y Alberto Rodríguez Piñón y que abriría la etapa Padel Pro Tour. “Me dediqué a organizar torneos amateurs, eventos por equipos, actividades sociales… Además, teníamos un departamento de construcción e instalaciones deportivas y en aquellos años llegamos a construir más de 1.000 pistas e invertimos en Alemania, Francia y otros países”, narra sobre el paso al lado y el cambio de la pista por un despacho, de la pala por el móvil y el ordenador. Casi dos décadas de trabajo en silencio donde su nombre se iría diluyendo en lo mediático coincidiendo con el boom español, primero, y su definitiva explosión internacional después. Unos años en los que el apellido Semprún, aunque como un eco lejano, siempre ha sido venerado como un tótem en el pádel español generando admiración, respeto y algo de controversia por sus hazañas, influencia y un marcado carácter que no dejan indiferente. Y cuando parecía que su sitio estaba ya hecho, que seguiría viviendo esa vida donde como asegura le hace estar “mucho mejor en mi casa”, una niña le haría recuperar la ilusión por la competición. Con otra figura y otro rol así volvería a la élite, reconvertido en entrenador, pero sin perder el ímpetu ni los objetivos como se puede comprobar cada fin de semana en los banquillos. “He vuelto por Martina, porque es alguien diferente. Me han ofrecido trabajar con otros jugadores, he tenido otras propuestas antes, pero solo lo he hecho porque he visto en ella unas condiciones que me parecían extraordinarias y porque es una persona maravillosa”, se sincera sobre su regreso para sentarse en el banquillo de Martina Calvo, el nuevo gran talento del pádel femenino mundial. El ‘Huracán Martina’ ocupa la octava posición del ranking FIP y ha vivido en apenas año y medio un ascenso meteórico que le ha convertido en la jugadora más joven en ganar un título Premier Padel. Resultados rápidos que no nublan la visión de Semprún porque, para él, el éxito de Martina no radica, o no solo, en su juventud y personalidad. “Creo que hay una parte que tiene que ver con cómo es ella, que tiene una fuerza de voluntad fuera de lo común y una capacidad de trabajo anormal. Si a eso le sumas que, además, es muy, muy lista y quiere aprender…”, explica de la que, por su palabras, es algo más que una jugadora o una simple alumna. Un sentimiento mutuo que hace meses ya se podía palpar en palabras de la propia Martina Calvo cuando en una entrevista en MARCA no dudaría en ensalzar su figura. “Si no fuera por Pablo no estaría aquí sentada. Llevo en su club toda mi vida, creo que desde los 4 años y quizá con él desde los 10. Hace muchas cosas por mí y te diría que nunca lo he visto como una relación de entrenador-jugadora, va mucho más allá”, explicaba Calvo. Semprún, que ha vivido diferentes eras del pádel, ahora de nuevo en la primera plana no duda a la hora de pararse a reflexionar sobre la eclosión de su ‘ahijada’ y de otros perfiles jóvenes con los que es crítico por “todo lo que empieza a rodear el deporte”. Sí, una clara alusión a las redes sociales, la fama, seguidores, contratos millonarios y los egos mutuos y ajenos. “Muchas veces los deportistas dicen que quieren aprender y en realidad no quieren. No quieren escuchar las cosas que no les gustan. Pero Martina es diferente, su manera de ser es otra, viene muy bien educada de casa y creo que eso es clave porque es lista y se queda con las cosas”, detalla ensalzando, en varias ocasiones, “los valores como persona” de la navarra que para él son fundamentales y que ejemplifica en la figura de Rafa Nadal. Una relación entrenador y jugadora que ya es exitosa en el corto plazo y apunta a ambiciosa en el medio y largo, años en los que Semprún sabe que no estará. “No quiero entrenar a nadie más y tampoco creo que vaya a estar mucho tiempo. ¿Cuánto puede ser? Dos, tres o cuatro años máximo. Estaré mientras yo crea que sea necesario y solo hasta que termine mi trabajo que creo sé dónde nos tiene que llevar”, confirma sin titubeo ajeno a la tentación del éxito y el business o la exposición del mainstream. Y tiene claro cuál es el objetivo. Sí, el número uno, una meta que afronta sin miedo porque “tenemos opciones si nos respetan las lesiones”, pero a la que pone freno porque “lo importante es el camino y que dentro de veinte años pueda mirar atrás y no reprocharse nada”. Una forma de entender la carrera de Calvo con la certeza de saber que él no siempre va a estar en su banquillo, pero donde sí espera poder seguir siendo su “consejero de vida” para que “cuando tenga 28 o 29 años, pueda llamarme y decirme: Oye, vamos a tomar algo que quiero contarte cómo veo esto”. El camino de una joven Martina con 18 años todavía está empezando y apenas tiene una cuenta de resultados con un puñado de victorias y derrotas. Pero él, ya con más que alguna cana, prepara una futura despedida no sin pensar en grande. Y no hay objetivo mayor en el deporte que llegar “a ser olímpico”, esa ambición en la que cree firmemente porque “sería el colofón perfecto” mientras que recuerda la cantidad de veces que “amigos míos que han sido olímpicos siempre hablan de lo especial que son unos Juegos Olímpicos”. Es su naturaleza mirar por el pádel. Semprún conoce la industria y ha sido jugador, promotor, entrenador…, y por ello no ve solo un frame de la película, la observa entera y detecta que su deporte “goza de muy buena salud”. Sí, “gracias a la labor de Damm” para crear World Padel Tour y de Premier Padel después para expandir el deporte y que hoy le hacen tener una lectura positiva del presente y futuro que complementa con esa faceta casi sindical que ejerció como jugador apuntando a su gremio, el de atletas, porque ahora “falta liderazgo, no unión”. No lo puede evitar. Es así. La realidad que él vivió como estrella del deporte hace más de 30 años era distinta, pero ahora que todo ha cambiado tanto cree firmemente que “el jugador tiene que dedicarse a jugar y lo importante no es que tres o cuatro ganen un dineral, es que puedan vivir del deporte el jugador 60 o 70 del mundo”, finaliza antes de alarmar sobre la necesidad de que “los promotores dejen de perder dinero” y se encuentre el equilibrio en un pádel ya en ritmo de crucero. Se consiga o no, esté Semprún en primera, segunda o tercera línea, le veamos más o menos cerca del banquillo de Calvo, seguirá estando ahí. ¿Dónde le encontraremos? Difícil saberlo, probablemente en algún lugar perdido en Navarra, en alguno de sus clubes, "bajando a Madrid" o compitiendo “en abuelitos”, como le gusta decir, y habiendo vuelto a dar un paso atrás para seguir haciendo sus cosas, pero como siempre abierto a escuchar y ser escuchado para construir, algo que hizo siempre porque es su forma de ser y va en su carácter, ese mismo del que se cuestiona tantas veces sus formas, pero en el que en rara ocasión se pone en duda el fondo. Así es la historia del que para muchos es “el Severiano Ballesternos del pádel”. Así ha sido y es la carrera de alguien que, más que un jugador, fue un pionero que llegó casi de casualidad a este deporte y se atrevió a mirar más allá. Una figura poco común que desde hace décadas se ha ganado de muchas y variadas formas ser parte de la historia. Y claro que lo hizo porque pudo, pero también porque creyó en ello cuando pocos lo hacían, porque se atrevió y porque, además, supo aceptar su sitio cuándo y cómo tocaba demostrando una inteligencia rara en los deportistas de élite. Y, además, porque como él mismo asegura dejando clara su forma de competir, ser y vivir: “Joder, nunca dejé de explorar este camino por el miedo”. Y no esperábamos menos de este outsider del pádel.

articles.title: Mona Agarwal wins gold, becomes first Indian to win Asian Para Games medal in 50m rifle 3 positions
articles.summary: India's Mona Agarwal continued her golden run at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games, rewriting the world record to clinch her second gold medal of the
articles.body: India's Mona Agarwal continued her golden run at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games, rewriting the world record to clinch her second gold medal of the competition in the women's 50m rifle 3 Positions SH1 final on Friday. The Indian para shooter produced a record score of 357.5 to finish 3.8 points ahead of China's Cuiping Zhang, setting a new World Record and Asian Para Games Record.Mona's latest triumph came after she had already struck gold in the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 event on the opening day.Mona outguns Chinese rival as Avani misses podiumMona delivered a composed performance in the 50m rifle 3 Positions SH1 final to secure the gold medal with a world-record score of 357.5. China's Cuiping Zhang finished second to take silver, trailing the Indian by 3.8 points.India's other finalist, Avani Lekhara, narrowly missed out on a podium finish, ending fourth. Avani had been among the leading contenders after the prone position but lost ground during the standing series, which proved decisive in the final standings.Second gold after opening-day triumphMona had earlier teamed up with Avani for an Indian one-two finish in the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 event on the opening day. She won gold with a score of 250 after the seventh series, setting an Asian Para Games record and surpassing Avani's previous mark of 249.6 from the 2023 Hangzhou edition.India close in on best-ever Asian Para Games medal tallyMona's second gold came as India continued their push to surpass their previous best performance at the Asian Para Games. At the time of reporting, India had collected 103 medals: 27 gold, 33 silver and 43 bronze and stood fourth in the overall standings, with China leading the table with 354 medals.India's record haul at the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Para Games was 111 medals.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Le quitan el carné de conducir y recurre a una falsificación para intentar correr dos rallyes
articles.standfirst: Con la falsificación, el investigado, un hombre de 27 años vecino de Langreo, pretendía correr dos rallyes en Asturias y que le devolviesen la licencia completa de piloto
articles.summary: Con la falsificación, el investigado, un hombre de 27 años vecino de Langreo, pretendía correr dos rallyes en Asturias y que le devolviesen la licencia completa de piloto
articles.body: La Guardia Civil está investigando a un vecino de Langreo (Asturias) que carecía de carné de conducir y que, según todos los indicios, habría falsificado un documento de la DGT para correr dos rallyes de coches y ampliar su licencia de piloto, que estaba restringida. Según informa Europa Press, el investigado habría hecho una falsificación mediante herramientas digitales para simular que ya estaba en posesión del carné. Este requisito resulta imprescindible debido a que muchos rallyes tienen enlaces por carretera y pasan por vías abiertas al tráfico, por lo que están sujetos al Reglamento General de Circulación y se exige el carné B. Además, el hombre, de 27 años, habría solicitado que le devolvieran la licencia completa en sustitución de la restringida con la que contaba (esta se aplica cuando el conductor no tiene licencia de conducir), lo que exige estar en posesión del mencionado carné B. El falso documento fue presentado ante la Federación Automovilística del Principado de Asturias (FAPA) para formalizar la inscripción y cambiar su licencia a completa. Pero esta federación pidió a la Jefatura Provincial de Tráfico que comprobase la autenticidad de la documentación, la cual detectó que aquellos datos no coincidían con los registros de la DGT y puso el asunto en manos del Grupo de Investigación y Análisis de Tráfico (GIAT). 23 días duraron las investigaciones, tras lo cual se determinó no solo que el supuesto documento oficial era falso, sino también que el autor de dicho documento contaba con un amplio historial por conducir sin carné. Ahora, todo el asunto está en manos del Tribunal de Instancia de Oviedo.

articles.title: A Wink and a Smile: Jarvis Returns, but Hurricanes Are Done in by Oilers Power Play Dominance
articles.summary: Well, the Carolina Hurricanes’ 6-5 shootout loss to the Edmonton Oilers was certainly not short of action, storylines, and…controversy. Because […]
articles.body:
Well, the Carolina Hurricanes' 6-5 shootout loss to the Edmonton Oilers was certainly not short of action, storylines, and…controversy. Because even late October, cross-conference games can have some controversy, eh?

The Storyline: Return of the 'Manitoba Mad Man'

Seth Jarvis, the Hurricanes' leading goal scorer for the past two seasons, made his return to play after being activated from the injured reserve Wednesday afternoon – his first game back since undergoing surgery to repair his shoulder. Quite frankly, upon his return, he didn't seem to miss a beat from my view behind the screens. Midway through the game, he even got the Hurricanes a go-ahead goal!

But, from his own perspective, he spoke on what he felt was a lacking game from himself – and in classic Jarvis fashion, pinned the loss onto himself.

"One of my biggest things is defense, and being responsible," he said after the game, "and I thought that part was kinda lacking tonight, and that's a big reason why we didn't kinda pull this one out."

Before I dig into the action of the game, let's get into the controversy – because I know that is likely one of the reasons you are still reading.

Of course, it wasn't anything massive – nothing like chanting disdain for a player or throwing the sweater of said player onto the ice en masse – but it was certainly an eyebrow raiser.

In the third period, Zach Hyman took a shove from K'Andre Miller, dropping to one knee as he tried to maintain his hold on the puck. During that slide, Sean Walker put a little check to the upper back of Hyman. In response, Hyman…played it up, sprawling onto the ice, sliding on his face, and remaining there as if badly injured. The referee pretty quickly called a cross-checking penalty on Walker, who was understandably irate due to the lack of severity of his hit – and the clear embellishment on Hyman's part.

As for Hyman? He, in fact, got up just fine, looking at his teammate and giving a wink and a smile – something caught by the Hurricanes' broadcast. Needless to say, people on social media were pretty quick to share their opinions on the matter.

Embellishment much?🤨 Zach Hyman took a little tap from Sean Walker and went sliding along the ice, seeming to have been in pain…once Walker got penalized, Hyman looked up at his teammate with a smile and a wink #CarolinaCulture #LetsGoOilers #NHL pic.twitter.com/mTD1WlVvog — Queen of the Puck (@rbarkleyhockey) October 23, 2026

Embellishment much?🤨 Zach Hyman took a little tap from Sean Walker and went sliding along the ice, seeming to have been in pain…once Walker got penalized, Hyman looked up at his teammate with a smile and a wink #CarolinaCulture #LetsGoOilers #NHL pic.twitter.com/mTD1WlVvog

Queen of the Puck (@rbarkleyhockey) October 23, 2026

"League should suspend players for this. Protect Integrity. We are one wink closer to soccer folks." said one hockey fan.

"Stripe's gotta help'em out B Freakin S" said another.

"Cross check to the neck of a guy who's already down, but sure." said one, pointing out the hit itself.

And finally, let's get into the action of the game, shall we?

The first period saw a power play goal apiece, with Leon Draisaitl scoring first , soon followed by Jackson Blake to tie things up . As a brief correction, the linked clip post lists the goal as Blake's 100th point. It was, in fact, only his 99th – a failure to verify the stat on my end of things during coverage.

That makes NHL point number 100! Jackson Blake nets his first power play goal of the season, and reaches a massive career milestone in doing so! #CarolinaCulture #LetsGoOilers #NHL pic.twitter.com/Lvqwdh3IkA — Queen of the Puck (@rbarkleyhockey) October 23, 2026

That makes NHL point number 100! Jackson Blake nets his first power play goal of the season, and reaches a massive career milestone in doing so! #CarolinaCulture #LetsGoOilers #NHL pic.twitter.com/Lvqwdh3IkA

As for the second period, it saw three even-strength Hurricanes goals – one by Sebastian Aho , an ever stylish one by Jarvis , and one by Logan Stankoven . Additionally, Ryan Nugent-Hopkins also scored on the power play.

SETH FREAKIN' JARVIS! In his first game back after having his shoulder repaired, he lit the lamp with STYLE, breaking some metaphorical ankles with a slick little defensive move before finding twine #CarolinaCulture #LetsGoOilers #NHL pic.twitter.com/V0LSn83mWa — Queen of the Puck (@rbarkleyhockey) October 23, 2026

SETH FREAKIN' JARVIS! In his first game back after having his shoulder repaired, he lit the lamp with STYLE, breaking some metaphorical ankles with a slick little defensive move before finding twine #CarolinaCulture #LetsGoOilers #NHL pic.twitter.com/V0LSn83mWa

In the third period, the Oilers got their first (and only) even-strength goal of the night, by Connor McDavid , just 26 seconds into the frame – seconds after the Oilers lost Mattias Ekholm to injury . A couple of minutes later, Draisaitl lit the lamp yet again – tying the game on the power play acquired by Hyman and his aforementioned shenanigans.

Juuso Valimaki, though, found the back of the net for his first goal in a Hurricanes sweater, giving his team the lead.

Juuso Valimaki get his first goal as a member of the Carolina Hurricanes to grab the lead! It is his first NHL goal since December 10, 2024! #CarolinaCulture #LetsGoOilers #NHL pic.twitter.com/iG1N6JZYwi — Queen of the Puck (@rbarkleyhockey) October 23, 2026

Juuso Valimaki get his first goal as a member of the Carolina Hurricanes to grab the lead! It is his first NHL goal since December 10, 2024! #CarolinaCulture #LetsGoOilers #NHL pic.twitter.com/iG1N6JZYwi

In the waning minutes of the game, Hyman thought he'd scored the game-tying goal with goaltender Devon Levi back on the bench – but it was quickly poofed away by the refs due to a highstick. Nonetheless, McDavid scored soon after anyway , sending it to overtime.

After a scoreless additional frame, the shootout commenced , with Nugent-Hopkins being the only player to find twine.

The Carolina Hurricanes and Edmonton Oilers went to the shootout after a scoreless extra frame in overtime, with the only player to find the back of the net being Ryan Nugent-Hopkins, securing the win for the Oilers Great goaltending from both teams here The full moment:… pic.twitter.com/6f53HhRZJu — Queen of the Puck (@rbarkleyhockey) October 23, 2026

The Carolina Hurricanes and Edmonton Oilers went to the shootout after a scoreless extra frame in overtime, with the only player to find the back of the net being Ryan Nugent-Hopkins, securing the win for the Oilers Great goaltending from both teams here The full moment:… pic.twitter.com/6f53HhRZJu

The Hurricanes still left with a point, with their next game – versus the St. Louis Blues – being the final of their Western Conference road trip.
