articles.summary: The trial of seven healthcare professionals accused of negligence in Maradona’s death concludes, December verdict set.
articles.body:
The verdict in the trial over the 2020 death of Argentinian football legend Diego Maradona will be delivered on December 22, the court announced Thursday, after six months of hearings.

The trial of seven healthcare professionals accused of negligence in the star’s death concluded on Thursday with brief statements from Maradona’s daughter and several of the defendants.

“I hope my father receives the justice he deserves … like anyone else,” said Dalma Maradona, her voice breaking with emotion.

The main defendant in the case, Leopoldo Luque, Maradona’s primary doctor, declared: “I am innocent.”

Maradona died at age 60 from heart failure coupled with pulmonary oedema.

The larger-than-life star, who had a history of substance abuse, was found dead in his bed on November 25, 2020.

He was at his residence in Tigre, north of Buenos Aires, rented for his convalescence following minor neurosurgery.

His death plunged the country into mourning in the midst of the COVID-19 pandemic.

Lawyers for Maradona’s doctor say he was made ‘scapegoat’

The trial , which began in April, included testimony from more than 70 witnesses.

Prosecutors requested prison sentences ranging from four to 12 years for six of the seven defendants, with the heaviest sentence – 12 years – sought for Luque.

In closing arguments on Wednesday, Luque’s defence lawyers rejected the prosecution’s argument that Maradona’s death was foreseeable, calling their client a “ scapegoat ” in the case.

Throughout the trial, Luque was by far the most combative defendant, speaking several times when he felt he was being implicated.

His legal team played audio recordings, presented scientific articles and even a video of Maradona’s autopsy, provoking the anger of the footballer’s daughters.

“It’s easy to attack me because I’m the one who had the most contact with Maradona,” Luque said in court, asserting that “the only one who would defend me would be Diego.

“I cared deeply for him, I loved him, he was my idol and my friend,” he said.

The case has revolved around whether the doctors’ decision to allow Maradona to convalesce in a private home, instead of in a hospital, was negligent.

The prosecution pointed to the near-total absence of medical equipment, such as a hospital bed, defibrillator or a quickly available ambulance, as evidence of what they presented as the defendants’ dereliction of duty .

Several medical experts testified that Maradona’s caretakers failed to react to key warning signs – he was suffering from oedema, tachycardia and had difficulty breathing – in the lead-up to his death.

articles.title: VJ Edgecombe responds after LeBron James elbowed him in the nose during 76ers vs Cavaliers
articles.summary: VJ Edgecombe was left with a bloody nose after an accidental elbow by LeBron James during the Philadelphia 76ers’ win over the Cleveland Cavaliers. The Sixer...
articles.body:
VJ Edgecombe was left with a bloody nose after an accidental elbow by LeBron James during the Philadelphia 76ers' win over the Cleveland Cavaliers.

The Sixers were involved in an eventful game at home. They got off to a rough start and were even booed by their own supporters at one stage.

However, they turned it around in the end in fine fashion, with Edgecombe playing his part despite injuring his nose.

VJ Edgecombe jokes LeBron James could've bought him a new nose if the injury was serious

Jarrett Allen of the Cavaliers missed a free throw when there were just four minutes left in the frame.

As he almost always is, James rose high to get his hands on the ball, but he was pushed from behind by Donovan Mitchell, and that led to a loose-ball foul call.

During that action, when The King was pushed while up in the air, his left elbow caught Edgecombe flush in the nose, and he appeared to be in a lot of pain.

Thankfully, the 21-year-old was not too badly hurt and was able to continue. After the game, he confirmed that there was no serious injury before cracking a joke.

He said: "Thank God there's nothing bad, but if it was, he (LeBron James) could buy me a new nose.

"I can walk. I can shoot. I can see a little bit for right now… I'm going to play regardless. It's just a little blood running out."

Edgecombe's nose will make the headlines, but his performance against the Cavaliers deserves a lot of praise.

The 21-year-old scored 11 points, seven rebounds and picked up six assists to help the Sixers overturn a 29-point deficit to win the game.

articles.title: Baltimore Orioles Face Complications in MLB's Proposed Salary Cap Plan
articles.summary: A cap could restrain two high-spending rivals, while a floor could give the pennant-winning Rays far more room to grow.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Orioles finished 79-82 in 2026 and missed the playoffs for a second straight year. After winning the AL East in 2023, Baltimore now has to make up ground in a division that had three teams in the postseason this year. Orioles president of baseball operations Mike Elias acknowledged after the season that the results need to improve.

One team Baltimore must catch is also the division's lowest spender. The Tampa Bay Rays went 98-64, then beat Cleveland in Game 6 of the AL Championship Series on Monday to reach the World Series. New York made the playoffs as well, while Boston took an AL Wild Card spot.

Baseball's next labor agreement could change the financial picture in the AL East. Major League Baseball proposed a $245.3 million payroll cap and a $171.2 million floor for 2027. Under that plan, clubs above the cap would have to reduce spending and those below the floor would have to raise it.

MLB's Opening Day example listed Tampa Bay among teams below the floor and New York and Toronto above the cap. Baltimore appeared on neither list. Spotrac's 2026 payroll tracker puts the Orioles at $167.0 million, 17th in baseball and only about $4.2 million shy of the proposed floor. Tampa Bay ranked 28th at $95.6 million, roughly $75.6 million below it.

If a similar floor became part of the new agreement, Baltimore would not need to add much spending to clear that mark. The reigning AL champions would face a much larger jump. The Rays won 19 more regular-season games than the Orioles in 2026 while spending about $71.4 million less by Spotrac's measure.

There is a potential benefit for Baltimore at the other end. Spotrac lists the New York Yankees at $308.3 million and the Toronto Blue Jays at $276.1 million in 2026 payroll. A simple comparison puts them about $63.0 million and $30.8 million above the proposed cap.

A ceiling on those rivals could give the Orioles a better chance to compete for players and close a spending gap with New York. But the same system could require Tampa Bay to put considerably more money into an already successful roster. Toronto's high payroll did not produce a playoff berth in 2026, but the Blue Jays dealt with injuries and down years after the 2025 pennant.

Rosters and contracts can also change before any new rules take effect, and Baltimore still has its own work to do. Elias has pointed to the need for better results from a group that includes Pete Alonso, Gunnar Henderson and Jackson Holliday as its core. A floor so close to the Orioles' 2026 payroll would do little by itself to address that need. More productive spending would matter more than clearing a minimum.

The MLB Players Association opposes a cap system , and no cap or floor has been agreed to. For now, Baltimore needs to build a team capable of beating the Rays, regardless of how much the Yankees and Blue Jays are allowed to spend.

articles.title: Bruins Postgame: DiPietro’s First Shutout Means So Much More
articles.summary: The Boston Bruins had plenty to celebrate on Thursday night, but Michael DiPietro’s night meant much more than two points. […]
articles.body:
The Boston Bruins had plenty to celebrate on Thursday night, but Michael DiPietro 's night meant much more than two points.

The Bruins (8-2-1) extended their point streak to seven games with a commanding 6-0 win over the Nashville Predators (3-3-3) at TD Garden. Five different players scored, with David Pastrnak scoring twice and Casey Mittelstadt , Elias Lindholm , JJ Peterka , and Mark Kastelic adding one. Charlie McAvoy finished with four assists, and DiPietro made 28 saves in his first NHL shutout.

The Bruins hosted Hockey Fights Cancer night on Thursday. DiPietro lost his mother to cancer when he was younger, making his first NHL shutout on Thursday all the more meaningful.

"A little bit stressed out, but obviously, you couldn't really write it better," DiPietro said postgame. "For me, it means a lot on Hockey Fights Cancer night. My mom passed away when I was five from cancer. So for me, it means a lot, but also to my family and everyone back home, and I just want to make them proud, and obviously this is a really special moment."

DiPietro made stops on all 28 shots he faced, including seven high-danger shots. He finished with 3.78 goals saved above expected, according to Natural Stat Trick .

After the game, the Bruins greeted their goaltender with a shower of water from their bottles.

"I mean, what an awesome kid," McAvoy, 28, said about DiPietro, 27. "Getting to know him last year through camp. And then this year, kind of knowing that he was going to have a spot on the team, which he earned. But man, all through camp, just some of the saves that he was making, just so impressive. Tonight to get his first shutout, you know, coming off the heels of his first win in Anaheim, it's amazing."

DiPietro recorded his first NHL win last time out, and in his first start at home, recorded his first NHL shutout. He has played 100:17 without allowing a goal, with stops on each of his last 41 shots.

"Of course, yeah. I think it starts creeping in your head," DiPietro said when asked if the shutout was on his mind. "You're on an island out there for a long time, so a bunch of thoughts come [to] your head. So I think just kind of acknowledging it, kind of moving on from it, and just trying to stay as present as possible and not trying to get too far ahead of yourself is important, and just kind of resetting after each whistle."

"The team had a great start. I just wanted to make sure that I was sharp whenever the pucks were coming."

After his first NHL win, Michael DiPietro said that he was not going to let the puck out of his sight. So what about after his first NHL shutout? "Oh, I think this one might be under the pillow tonight like the other one, but yeah, definitely not letting this one out of my… pic.twitter.com/qyXc6tQ9pQ — Jack Studley (@jackstudley13) October 23, 2026

After his first NHL win, Michael DiPietro said that he was not going to let the puck out of his sight. So what about after his first NHL shutout? "Oh, I think this one might be under the pillow tonight like the other one, but yeah, definitely not letting this one out of my… pic.twitter.com/qyXc6tQ9pQ

Jack Studley (@jackstudley13) October 23, 2026

The last time the Bruins returned home from a trip out west, they came out flat and lost 4-1 to the Ottawa Senators. Marco Sturm harped on that after morning skate, but cited the Bruins coming out with "a good jump" on Thursday morning. That carried over into the game, as Casey Mittelstadt opened the scoring just 3:49 into the first period.

The Bruins took a 2-0 lead into the first intermission and added two goals in every period, a much different response than their last return home.

"You know what I liked the most, besides Mikey's shutout, is that we came out with energy," Sturm said after the game. "We talked about it in the morning. We addressed it. After a big road trip, it's not always easy, but I thought it was one of the best pre-game skates we had all year. That's exactly the way we skated – the energy, anything about it – we kind of carried it over to tonight's game. And that's where I'm happy with because now it shows for next time that we can do it. It's just a mindset. Sometimes it's hard, but that, for me, was the biggest reason why we won this game tonight."

The Bruins got off to a strong start and never wavered. They, like for much of the road trip, got contributions up and down their lineup. Five different Bruins found the back of the net, and they had two players with four-point nights. David Pastrnak, who had two goals and two assists on Thursday, now leads the team with six goals, but he's one of seven players to have three or more tucks this season.

"It's amazing. Obviously it helps [that] every line is producing," Pastrnak said. "It's more like you're waiting, just, 'Who is it going to be tonight?' So it's fun to see. Every line is finding chemistry already, slowly. So we have good chemistry all around four lines, and it's producing, so it's good to see and makes it much easier for us defending and getting the wins."

"It's been good. I think, especially when you kind of want to match lines or something," JJ Peterka, another goal scorer on Thursday, added. "When every line is capable of scoring goals, every line is dangerous when they're out there, and I think that's a really nice thing to have."

The Bruins now have points in their last seven games, including a 6-3 win over the San Jose Sharks last Tuesday. They will close out their season series, and their brief two-game homestand, against the Sharks on Saturday night at 7:00 PM.

articles.title: Here's when Mercedes could win their ninth F1 Constructors' title
articles.summary: Mercedes are moving closer to securing their ninth Formula 1 Constructors' Championship, having established a commanding advantage over their rivals througho...
articles.body:
Mercedes are moving closer to securing their ninth Formula 1 Constructors' Championship, having established a commanding advantage over their rivals throughout the 2026 season. With the campaign entering its final six rounds, the Silver Arrows are now approaching the point at which they could mathematically seal the title, but several scenarios remain possible.

The German manufacturer currently leads the standings with 578 points, ahead of Ferrari on 444, McLaren on 339 and Red Bull on 332. Mercedes have claimed 11 victories in the opening 17 Grands Prix, with Kimi Antonelli and George Russell occupying the top two positions in the Drivers' Championship.

A ninth Constructors' Championship would be Mercedes' first since 2021, when the team secured its eighth consecutive title. However, the championship cannot be decided at this weekend's United States Grand Prix, regardless of the results in Austin.

What does Mercedes need to secure the championship?

With six races remaining and no further Sprint events scheduled, a maximum of 258 points is still available in the Constructors' Championship. Each team can collect up to 43 points per Grand Prix by finishing first and second.

Even if Antonelli and Russell secure a one-two finish in Austin while both Ferrari drivers fail to score, Mercedes' advantage would only increase to 177 points. That would not be enough to settle the championship, as 215 points would remain available over the final five rounds.

Mexico City, on 1 November, therefore represents the first mathematical opportunity for Mercedes to claim the title. Following that race, only 172 points will remain available, meaning the Silver Arrows must leave Mexico with an advantage that Ferrari cannot overturn.

For Mercedes to achieve that, they would need to extend their current lead by at least 38 points across the United States and Mexican Grands Prix. Even in the most favourable scenario in Austin, with Mercedes scoring 43 points and Ferrari none, the Italian team would still need to be prevented from recovering the deficit in Mexico.

Mercedes have outscored Ferrari by an average of 7.6 points per Grand Prix this season. If that trend continues, the championship could instead be decided at the São Paulo Grand Prix on 8 November, when just 129 points would remain available.

Antonelli could become world champion before Mercedes

While Mercedes must wait until at least Mexico to secure the Constructors' Championship, Antonelli could wrap up the Drivers' title at this weekend's United States Grand Prix.

The Italian currently leads team-mate Russell by 102 points, with Lewis Hamilton a further nine points behind. With 150 points still available across the remaining six races, Antonelli has his first opportunity to secure the championship in Austin.

To do so, the 20-year-old must win the race, with Russell finishing ninth or lower and Hamilton fifth or lower. Such a result would make Antonelli the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history, surpassing Sebastian Vettel's record from 2010.

articles.title: Dayot Upamecano lauds Bayern Munich teammate Harry Kane
articles.summary: FC Bayern’s star center-back cannot say enough about Harry Kane.
articles.body:
Harry Kane continues to make his case as one of the best players in world football, and his latest performance against Arsenal has earned him high praise from his Bayern Munich teammate, Dayot Upamecano.

Kane recorded a goal and an assist in Bayern's 2-2 draw against the Gunners, once again demonstrating his importance to Vincent Kompany's side. Whether finishing chances himself or creating opportunities for his teammates, the England captain remains central to Bayern's attacking threat.

Upamecano was particularly emphatic when discussing Kane's quality, expressing his hope that the striker will eventually receive football's most prestigious individual award.

"Harry is Harry. Outstanding. I hope he wins the Ballon d'Or," Upamecano told Sky Germany's Kerry Hau (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ).

It is a simple statement, but one that reflects the admiration Kane has earned within the Bayern dressing room. His goalscoring numbers, creativity, and ability to influence major matches make him a compelling candidate for individual recognition.

Ultimately, winning the Ballon d'Or will depend on sustained performances and team success throughout the season. However, if Kane continues delivering against Europe's biggest clubs, he will give himself every opportunity to enter that conversation.

articles.title: Continuing To Improve The Cleveland Browns Heading Towards 2027 - Defensive Review
articles.summary: While I regularly write about next season and roster predictions, this looks more at what the team is likely to do. In this piece I want to focus on where th...
articles.body:
While I regularly write about next season and roster predictions, this looks more at what the team is likely to do. In this piece I want to focus on where the Browns need to improve to get to above average in each position room for 2027. It will focus much more on the starters rather than seeing anything in terms of depth.

They have a fantastic amount of cash and draft picks at their disposal to keep adding more to this young talented roster.

According to SūmerSports, the Cleveland Browns rank 11th in pressure rate and 7th in pressures generated as a defense this season. It is incredibly impressive when you consider they traded Myles Garrett and Alex Wright was injured. During the Andrew Berry era they have generally had a higher performing second edge, maybe Alex Wright can be that but it will depend how he bounces back from his injury. They will certainly be looking at drafting or adding more talent here in the offseason, their rotational depth is stacked, but they could do with a special player to lead the room, this will hopefully allow Verse to bounce back to his level with the Rams.

The Browns have a stud with Graham but the question is what to do with Maliek Collins. He is playing really well the last five weeks but he will also turn 32 just before the draft, so it might be one where we need to see how he finished the season before making a decision. At the same time Adin Huntington has jumped forward too in the last few weeks after a poor start to the season. They could run it back, but at the same time I can see them adding one more and operating from a position of strength with Collins as a dominant third defensive tackle. Then moving on from Hall or Huntington at the end of training camp. Whatever they do they will be in a strong position next season.

The two starters are fantastic and will return next season. They need to find a more reliable third linebacker. Easton Mascarenas-Arnold's 36 career defensive snaps haven't convinced me that he can step in and start if there is an injury. Maybe he gets a chance to prove his point during this season. You don't need to spend much here, around $2-3m can get you an experienced third linebacker that can also play special teams. They aren't needed for defensive play in this scheme as it is two linebacker heavy, but it gives you injury protection.

Around 66% of snaps they will play a third cornerback in the slot. This issue with Myles Harden is the inconsistency. You have times when he is great and others when he is really struggling. Ideally they will want a better player here as well as more depth for injuries behind Ward and Campbell. Blackmon was serviceable but where most teams don't have three good cornerbacks, the chances of having real depth are incredibly thin. If they can draft someone the develop on the boundary and add more experience in the slot via free agency, it will put them in an even stronger spot next season.

They will have a decision to make after the season of what to do with Hickman. Both Delpit and McNeil-Warren are here for the long term and will be starting next season. There has been a gentle increase in usage of a third safety with the team playing them 40-50% the last three weeks. This seems to be wider than just wanting to get McNeil-Warren on the field as it continued when Delpit went down and they brought Daniel Thomas in. This could open the door to keeping Hickman beyond this season, while Thomas played well, there is a benefit to having more depth. I can see them pushing to keep Hickman as long as he isn't wanting too much, especially if he is playing around 50% of snaps and providing quality depth at the same time.

I would expect the plan is to run it back. They could look to change their punter though if they are moving to being a top team. Corey Bojorquez's skill is flipping the field, if you are looking to punt and pin someone in deep, then there is probably someone else you can find. The fact they had three punters during camp and then one on the practice squad shows they want more.

After a rough week one start, it feels like his work has been exceptional. Despite losing a superstar in Myles Garrett they have spread the burden across the rest of the roster and everyone is stepping up. We will need to see it over a larger period but this feels like a very talented defensive coaching staff. Don't be shocked if defensive coordinators are hired from this group over the next few years.

The shopping list is very low, there are no desperate needs, more areas it would be nice to upgrade, such as:

Defensive Tackle Help (If Collins Slows)

It feels like the Browns are approaching an offseason where it is a quarterback and luxury picks/additions. It is important that they don't go and waste that advantage. The Chiefs should have taken Tee Higgins in the 2020 draft to add more weapons but thought a running back would help them more and selected Clyde Edwards-Helaire. Their struggle with pass catchers continues to this day where as they have found alternative backs fairly easily. While people regularly talk about 'best player available' the Browns could operate from that position in the 2027 draft.

It is why coming into this season I was incredibly high on the Browns in 2027 and I see no reason to pause the optimism.

articles.title: Iowa vs Minnesota Prediction: Can the Hawkeyes Keep Floyd?
articles.summary: Iowa vs Minnesota should be a great battle, made bigger by the winner getting a bronze pig. Here's the CFN preview and prediction.
articles.body:
In 1935, Iowa and Minnesota played for the rights to Floyd, a prize pig from Iowa, in an attempt to make the spicy border war rivalry a bit more fun. Minnesota won 13-6, the pig died, and a bronze statue was created to serve as the trophy for the winner. Minnesota won 52-0 in 1936 and got to keep the fake pig until Iowa finally broke the streak with a 13-9 win in 1939. This year, it means a little more. Iowa lost to Ohio State, but came back and ripped up Washington 41-24. With just one loss, it has a buffer – a 10-2 Iowa would absolutely get into the College Football Playoff. However, this might be the toughest remaining test. Minnesota couldn't hang with Purdue in a 41-13 loss, and it's one loss away from effectively being out of the CFP mix. But for now, just getting Floyd back would be good enough.

Iowa gets home games in two of the next three games, starting with Wisconsin and then going to Northwestern.

Minnesota keeps alternating the home and road games, going to Indiana next before hosting UCLA.

Iowa has owned the series lately, going 10-1 going back to 2014, with Minnesota's last win 12-10 in 2023.

Okay, Jeremy Hecklinski. Do that again. Out of nowhere, Hecklinski got off the plane in Seattle and completed 14-of-19 passes for 202 yards and three touchdowns in the win over Washington. That was good, but Kamari Moulton's 208 yards on the ground and two scores helped make it a rout. Minnesota couldn't handle Kamario Taylor's passing in the 38-13 loss to Mississippi State several weeks ago, and Fluff Bothwell's 113 rushing yards and two touchdowns made things even worse. Last week, the Gophers came out to stop Purdue quarterback Ryan Browne, and Fame Ijeboi ran for 193 yards and three touchdowns. However …

Yeah, Mississippi State and Purdue ripped up the Gopher defense. The running backs went off, but Kamario Taylor and Ryan Browne both ran wild to turn their respective games into a rout. Hecklinski has run twice for five yards, and fellow Iowa quarterback Hank Brown has rushed for just one score. Minnesota has to control the clock, the tempo, and the lines. It's No. 1 in the Big Ten in fewest sacks allowed, the pass rush is great, and when this team gets physical, look out.

Iowa vs Minnesota Prediction, Betting Lines

Never mess with a rivalry streak. The weather in Minneapolis will be absolutely perfect, and Iowa fans will expect the fireworks they got in the win over Washington. Minnesota won't let that happen. The Gophers will need Drake Lindsey to get hot from the start and hit his third down shots. The problem will be an Iowa pass rush that will bother him enough to keep that from happening. The lack of a steady Gopher running game will be glaring.

articles.title: How Thunder’s Shai Gilgeous-Alexander losing 20-point streak earned extra admiration from Mark Daigneault
articles.summary: OKLAHOMA CITY — With 1:43 left toward the end of a 96-84 win against the Denver Nuggets, Oklahoma City Thunder All-Star Shai Gilgeous-Alexander decided it wa...
articles.body:
OKLAHOMA CITY — With 1:43 left toward the end of a 96-84 win against the Denver Nuggets, Oklahoma City Thunder All-Star Shai Gilgeous-Alexander decided it was time to end his streak of scoring 20+ points in 141 consecutive regular-season games, head coach Mark Daigneault revealed. Amidst a cold shooting night, Gilgeous-Alexander found his offensive rhythm after halftime, scoring 13 of his 17 points in the second half against the Nuggets.

The two-time MVP drained a dagger 3-pointer that extended the Thunder's lead to 20 points (93-73), forcing Nuggets head coach David Adelman to empty his bench. That's when Gilgeous-Alexander turned to Daigneault, and asked to be subbed out of the game.

"It's a historic record. So, it's a bit of a dilemma if you're in my position," Daigneault said. "But he put me in a great position there. I would have left him. I was gonna leave him [in]. Just another reason on the list of why I admire him."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Thunder head coach Mark Daigneault adds Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's decision to be taken out of the game to a long list of things he admires about the two-time MVP. Daigneault commended Gilgeous-Alexander for making the call when he didn't have to.

"For the class that it shows and the perspective that it shows for him to say, "Hey, I'm out now, the game's calling for me to be subbed out of the game," that was his substitution, and of all the things that I admire about him, that's toward the top of the list in terms of moments that I appreciate about him," Daigneault said. "It shows tremendous class as a competitor."

For Gilgeous-Alexander, watching the Nuggets sub their starters out was all he needed to see to make the decision that his night was over, cementing a record that took over 60 years to break.

"I was gonna go out there. Then, I saw that they had subbed. So, I thought, we should sub, too," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "I feel like you always treat the game with respect. And God willing I have many more games to start another streak. So, it's not that important."

Thunder All-Star Chet Holmgren admitted he's not sure if he would have made the same choice if he were in Gilgeous-Alexander's shoes, but commends SGA for making the admirable decision.

"I asked him, I said, 'You want to shoot some threes right here,' and he's like, "Nah," then, he went up to Mark and subbed himself out," Holmgren said. "I told him he's a better man than me. I would have been shooting some pull-up threes. I think it was a selfless moment, and he's a selfless guy. He's one of the hardest workers that I know, and it shows up out there. And so does his leadership, and he does that the right way."

Gilgeous-Alexander was 6-for-19, including 3-for-11 from deep against the Nuggets. He also finished with three assists and one block. Jalen Williams' 21 points led the Thunder, while Holmgren finished with 17 rebounds, 12 points, and four blocks. Oklahoma City improved to 2-0 on the regular season.
